newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH 1996 BUDGET GAP COULD FALL BELOW 2.5 PCT.
newsitem.headline: POLISH 1996 BUDGET GAP COULD FALL BELOW 2.5 PCT.

text.p: Polish budget deficit could fall this year to below 2.5 percent of gross domestic product against the 1996 plan of 2.8 percent, mainly due to lower-than-planned debt servicing costs, Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko told a news briefing.

Kolodko told a group of foreign journalist that both this year's revenues and spending were likely to fall below the budget plan but that the difference in spending would be larger making a lower deficit possible.

"There is a shortfall from the budget projection both on the revenue and expenditure side but decidedly deeper with regard to spending...and therefore the budget deficit can be lower if this trend holds and could be below 2.5 percent or even at 2.43 percent (of GDP)," Kolodko said.

Kolodko said the main savings in the costs of public debt servicing would be a result of a combination of factors such as domestic and foreign interest rates, cross currency rates and joint treasury and central bank efforts to coordinate public debt management.

He also said subsidies to the social security system might prove slightly lower than originally anticiapated but stressed all areas would receive sufficient funding and the lower overall expenditures would be achieved without spending cuts.

After the first 10 months of this year the budget gap amounted to 6.4 billion zlotys or 63.1 percent of the planned 10.16 billion shortfall with revenues at 79.7 percent of the 1996 plan and spending at 78.2 percent of the plan.

Poland recorded a deficit of 2.7 percent of GDP last year and the government projects a shortfall of 2.6 percent or 2.8 percent next year depending on next year's tax scale, which the parliament is due to decide on Thursday.
